Requested Service: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial/unicompartmental knee replacement), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-24. I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated on that notice (deadline 2027-02-20).

1. The Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states that the request was denied because "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure," and that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." The notice does not name, number, or quote the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria document that was applied. I have been unable to locate any published Wisconsin Medicaid/ForwardHealth clinical policy that sets out procedure-specific medical-necessity criteria for CPT 27446. Because no such document was identified or quoted to me, I am not able to respond point-by-point to specific numbered criteria, and I am not going to guess at or restate criteria the plan has not actually shown me. I am therefore also formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that the plan:

- Identify by title, number, and effective date the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria relied upon to deny CPT 27446 in this case; and
- Provide a copy of that document, and of the reviewer's written rationale, so that the imaging and clinical findings below can be matched to the plan's actual stated criteria.

I note that Wisconsin Medicaid fair hearing procedures affirmatively recognize a member's "right, both before the hearing and during the hearing, to see the local agency's written materials about the case, including [the] case record, on which the local agency based its decision" (DHS Form F‑10151, Medicaid/BadgerCare Plus Fair Hearing Information). I am relying on that right in requesting the reviewer's rationale and any cited criteria.

2. Why the Imaging and Clinical Record Support Medical Necessity

Regardless of the specific named policy, Wisconsin's regulatory definition of "medically necessary" governs coverage of Medicaid services. Under Wis. Admin. Code § DHS 101.03(96m), a covered service must be:

"(a) Required to prevent, identify or treat a recipient's illness, injury or disability; and (b) ... 1. ... consistent with the recipient's symptoms or with prevention, diagnosis or treatment of the recipient's illness, injury or disability; 2. ... provided consistent with standards of acceptable quality of care applicable to the type of service, the type of provider and the setting in which the service is provided; 3. ... appropriate with regard to generally accepted standards of medical practice; 4. ... not medically contraindicated with regard to the recipient's diagnoses, the recipient's symptoms or other medically necessary services being provided to the recipient; 5. ... of proven medical value or usefulness and ... not experimental in nature; 6. ... not duplicative with respect to other services being provided to the recipient; 7. ... not solely for the convenience of the recipient, the recipient's family or a provider; 8. ... cost-effective compared to an alternative medically necessary service which is reasonably accessible to the recipient; and 9. ... the most appropriate supply or level of service that can safely and effectively be provided to the recipient."

The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies each of these elements:

- Imaging findings: MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-24 documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This is advanced, isolated (unicompartmental) degenerative joint disease — the specific pattern of disease that a partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement is designed to treat. The denial reasoning that "imaging findings... do not support medical necessity" is not consistent with these findings, which show severe, single-compartment, bone-on-bone disease.
- Symptom duration and severity: 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, with nighttime awakening 3–4 times per night due to pain and an inability to climb stairs without assistance — a clinically significant functional disability.
- Exhausted conservative treatment: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-05-26 through 2026-07-21, 20 visits completed) targeting quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 4 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-14 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. Conservative management has therefore been fully and adequately trialed and has failed to provide durable relief.
- Physical examination: Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, corroborating the imaging and symptom picture.
- Absence of contraindications: No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, and non-smoker status — none of which contraindicate surgery.

Taken together, this record documents a patient with advanced, isolated medial compartment osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, bone-on-bone), significant functional impairment, and a full trial of guideline-consistent conservative therapy (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) that has failed. This is the clinical picture for which unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (CPT 27446) is the medically appropriate, guideline-consistent next step in treatment.

3. Requested Action

I respectfully request that the plan:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27446; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide the specific named medical policy/clinical review criteria applied to this request, along with the reviewer's written rationale, so that this appeal can be supplemented directly against the plan's own stated criteria within the remaining appeal window.

Given the ongoing nightly pain, sleep disruption, and functional limitation described above, I also ask that this appeal be handled on an expedited basis to the extent permitted under Wisconsin Medicaid appeal procedures.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and/or email above. I authorize Dr. Duval's office to submit or discuss additional clinical documentation on my behalf if needed. [Attach separate Authorized Representative form if applicable.]

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21)
- MRI report dated 2026-07-24
- Office visit/examination notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-14)
